content.text:
Ceate an SVG of an awkward family portrait of robots. Give each robot a distinct personality, and suggest their relationships through poses and composition. No text.

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.11.1 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

content.thinking:
I will create an SVG family portrait of robots with distinct personalities and awkward poses.

I am checking the constraints. The deliverables must be under 2 MB each and videos under 10 seconds. I will keep source code in the working directory and delete intermediate files.

I will hand-craft the SVG rather than generate a raster image. The composition will capture classic awkward family portrait moments: forced smiles, someone standing too close, and someone looking away.

I am fleshing out the family cast. A fidgeting kid robot, a teenager with crossed arms, parents trying to pose formally, and a grandparent are all in the mix. I will use awkward arm gestures, uneven heights, and a glitchy "cheese" moment to show their personalities and relationships. The dad robot will be boxy and industrial, stiffly holding his wife.

The dad robot will have a welding-torch smile and a wire mustache. The mom robot is round and domestic with warm colors, holding the family together with one hand on her husband and another reaching toward a child who is pulling away. The teenager robot is sleek and angular in matte black with neon accents, slouching with crossed arms and a visor while being pulled into the group.

The little kid robot is small and colorful, sticking out a manipulator tongue and holding a toy wrench. The grandparent robot is vintage and rusty with huge optical sensors, sitting formally and slightly overlapping the dad. The baby robot squirms in its mother's arms and looks at the ceiling.

A family dog robot joins the cast. It sits awkwardly and looks at a squirrel off-camera, or has a wall-eye stare at the camera. The backdrop is a classic studio portrait with mottled blue and gray tones, or a living room with a crooked picture frame and wallpaper. The pyramid arrangement is lopsided and slightly off-center.

The portrait will suggest a flash photograph with harsh, flat lighting and a slightly tilted frame. I am adding specific awkwardness cues: misaligned eyelines, a forced arm-around-shoulder that the recipient is leaning away from, gaps where someone should stand closer, overlapping in uncomfortable ways, a tangled cable between two robots, and the teenager's foot on the dog.

I am adding more specific awkwardness details. The grandpa's antenna will bonk the dad's head. The baby will stick its arm in the mom's face. The kid will make rabbit ears behind the teenager or dad. One robot will have a straight LED smile while others curve theirs. A studio stool will be too small for the grandpa. Only one sensor will show a flash reflection. The heights will not stair-step neatly. A shadow will not match the light source. One robot will be mid-blink with an eyelid half down. I am designing this as a polished illustration rather than a crude diagram.

The illustration will use flat colors and subtle gradients with consistent line weight. A landscape composition at roughly 1200 by 800 pixels will let the awkward spacing between robots remain visible.

The palette is now defined. The studio backdrop will be dusty teal and sage mottled with a beige carpet floor. Dad will be steel blue-gray with a proud chest plate and thick arms. Mom will use warm copper and cream tones with soft curves and a pearl-like sensor necklace. The teenager will be charcoal with magenta LED accents and a slim hoodie-like cowl. The child will be primary yellow and orange with round sticker-like panel decals. Grandpa will be olive drab and brass with rivets and a monocle lens. The baby will be pastel mint and spherical. The dog will be a chrome beagle with floppy antenna ears.

I am sketching the exact placement of each robot. The grandpa sits on a too-small stool in the back left. Dad stands tall and stiff in the back right. Mom holds the baby on her hip in the center, with the baby reaching toward dad's face. The teenager slouches beside mom, and the kid stands in front making faces.

The teenager stands apart with a dead stare, shrugging off mom's hand. The child stands on tiptoes with a wink and a metal tab tongue. The dog faces the camera but its head is cranked ninety degrees at something off-frame, frozen mid-wag.

The dad's arm around mom is a misjudged clamp, resting too high on her head. The mom leans away while trying to corral the teenager with her other arm. The teenager steps out of reach, weight on one leg. Grandpa photobombs with his tilted head and accidentally places his cane between the dad's legs. The kid stands on the dad's foot, slightly bent. The baby bonks the mom's optical sensor with its arm.

The dog's leash wraps around the grandpa's cane. The group is left-clustered with awkward empty space on the right. A studio plant in the corner looks dying. The backdrop seam shows a wrinkle in the paper.

The dad and grandpa share a similar face design, but the dad is clearly uncomfortable with it. The teenager inherits the mom's round optical housing and the dad's angular jaw, creating a family resemblance. The child robot is a chaotic mix of parts from everyone, like a hand-me-down that looks like a patchwork. I am now defining the personalities: the grandpa robot is Unit-0, proud and obsolete, refusing to update, with huge earnest eyes and a wire bow tie.

The dad robot is an anxious middle-manager bot with an overcompensating posture, a too-wide LED smile, and a crooked tie. He is trying to perform as a good father. The mom robot is the glue of the family, showing a warm but slightly exhausted half-smile while organizing everyone with both hands. The teenager robot is too cool, with a raised eyebrow panel and a dead stare at the camera, clearly embarrassed to be there. The kid robot has gremlin energy.

The child robot will leave muddy wheel tracks on the carpet. The baby will drool a drop of oil and grab the mother's antenna. The dog will sit on the father's foot with a cooling fin out, looking cross-eyed at a fly. The illustration will use metallic gradients, subtle drop shadows, rivets, panel lines, and consistent strokes.

I will hand-author the SVG directly for better visual quality. I am checking the workspace and available tools. Python cannot easily rasterize SVG, so a PNG render may not be possible.

I will deliver the SVG directly, since no external rendering tools are available. A subtle animated video is also an option.

An animated SVG or GIF would capture the awkwardness of a long exposure, with subtle blinking, swaying, and tail wagging. I am checking the environment for built-in rendering tools, but no external packages are available.

The SVG canvas will be 1600 by 1100 pixels in landscape. The studio background will use a vertical gradient from cool teal to warm gray, a slightly curling paper seam, and a mottled beige floor. Soft contact shadows will sit beneath each robot.

A visible light stand at the edge will add meta-awkwardness. The teenager robot is named Vex. He is medium-tall but slouches to appear shorter. His body is charcoal gray with dark panels and half-lidded magenta LED eyes. He stands with arms tightly crossed, a hip cocked, and one foot turned out.

The teenager robot has a dangling wire from one earbud and a scuffed shoulder where the mom's hand almost reaches but stops twenty pixels short. His optical sensor is round like his mother's, and his jaw is rectangular like his father's. The grandpa robot is named Rust and sits on a tiny wooden studio stool with knees raised high.

Rust’s palette is faded sage, brass, and rust spots. He has a tall boxy head with two wide-open eyes, a wire bow tie, and a white mustache made of curved rods. One arm rests on his knee while the other stiffly holds a cane that crosses in front of dad’s shin. His antenna ball tip is cropped by the frame or pokes dad’s shoulder. He smiles small and polite but slightly crooked. Rivets cover his body and a patch panel is visible. One eye lens is frosted like a cataract.

The dad robot is named Chief. He is tall and rectangular in navy and steel gray. His chest puffs and his shoulders square off in an attempt to look strong. His LED smile is too wide and grid-like, slightly crooked, with a single prong of a three-prong clamp hovering on mom’s shoulder. One eye is wide with anxiety. An oil sweat drop sits on his temple. His geometric tie is crooked. His left arm hangs stiff and closed. His left foot rests under the child.

The mom robot is named Ada. She is a softer trapezoid torso in copper and cream, standing between dad and teen. Her amber eyes are tired with lowered upper lids, and she wears a string of pearl-like spherical sensors around her neck. Her hair is a rounded bob of brushed metal plates or coiled wire. She reaches gently toward the teenager with her left arm while cradling the baby with her right.

Ada carries a single earring and a soft apron-like panel. The baby robot Bit is mint and white with huge eyes fixed on the studio light above, not the camera. He reaches upward with one arm while pulling at his mother’s pearl necklace with the other, kicking out a leg, and sporting a single curl antenna.

The baby robot Bit will drool a drop of oil and carry a simple geometric diaper panel.

A new front-center character named Sprocket is added. He is short and round in bright yellow and orange. His arms are mismatched: one is steel blue from the dad, the other copper from the mom. He winks with one eye closed in a > shape while the other eye stays wide. A pink-orange metal tongue sticks out. One hand reaches behind the dad to do rabbit ears, with fingers visible beside his head. The other hand rests on his hip in a superhero pose. He stands with feet apart and one foot on the dad's shoe.

Sprocket will have scuffed knees and a small band-aid patch on his cheek. He grins chaotically with a propeller beanie and carries a tiny toy robot in one hand.

Bolt the dog sits low on the right in chrome and white with a black nose sensor. One ear is flipped up to reveal its copper underside. He looks at a fly or the plastic plant with his head turned right, mouth open and tongue out.

Bolt’s tail is a spring antenna curved upward. He sits on a tangled cable leash that runs across the floor behind everyone, crossing grandpa’s cane. One eye catches a bright white flash disk while the other stays normal. His collar tag is blank.

The composition is left-heavy: empty carpet and a plastic fern occupy the right third where the dog looks. The teenager stands forty pixels apart, creating a visible personal-space wedge. Grandpa’s seated posture and tiny stool make his head nearly as tall as the standing dad, so the heads sit at uneven heights rather than a clean stair step.

The child’s rabbit ears will peek into the dad’s head silhouette. The baby’s raised arm will graze the mother’s face. The grandpa’s cane diagonal will form a visual trip line. The backdrop seam will fall directly behind the dad’s head. The dog’s shadow will angle slightly off from the flash direction, adding a subtle lighting inconsistency. The teen’s left elbow and the dog’s tail will be cropped by the frame edges. The grandpa’s antenna tip will touch the top edge. A single red “on” LED on the dad will signal his nervousness.

A colored floor tape mark will sit between the parents, but the child stands off it while the dad’s foot rests on it. A second person’s reflection may appear in the grandpa’s optical sensor lens.

The studio will use a very subtle vignette and soft grain. A printed-photo frame with uneven margins was considered but rejected. The image will fill the SVG cleanly without extra framing.

The SVG viewBox is fixed at 1600 by 1000. Head coordinates are now mapped to specific x and y positions across the frame. The cyc wall curves from y=560, the floor runs from y=640 to 1000, and the child robot sits lowest at y=620 so his feet overlap the parents’ legs.

Adult robots will be roughly 520 pixels tall for readability. Each character is built from grouped shapes using a consistent construction method. Head types vary by family line: vertical rounded rectangles for the grandpa and dad, circles or ovals for the mom and baby, a hybrid rounded rectangle with circular eye housing for the teen, a circle head with a dad-style chin bolt for the kid, and a horizontal oval for the dog. The grandpa’s eyes are huge circles with small pupils pinned forward, and his left lens is hazy.

The dad’s pupils are forward with lots of white, and his eyebrows are raised in the middle. The mom’s pupils stay forward but her eyelids sit at thirty percent. The teen’s pupils glance slightly left while a magenta glow surrounds half-closed horizontal slits. The kid keeps one eye as a big circle and the other as a wink chevron. The baby’s eyes sparkle upward. The dog’s eyes are mismatched, one fixed on the plant. The grandpa’s mouth is a small straight grille with a slight upturn. The dad’s mouth shows too many wide tooth rectangles. The mom’s mouth is a gentle short arc. The teen’s mouth is a single flat slot.

The kid robot will show an open smile with its tongue out. The baby robot will have a small oval mouth. The dog robot will pant with an open mouth.

A Python script will generate the SVG to keep the source code in ./src/ and the finished image in ./output/.

A PNG render will be included alongside the SVG for broader compatibility. The art direction is a stiff, awkward Sears portrait of mid-century tin toy robots in clean editorial vector style with soft studio lighting and flat cel shading. It avoids cute overload and grimdark tones.

The wink will sit on the side of the tongue for a cohesive silly face. Dad’s eyebrows will be thick and worried, with inner brows raised. Mom’s brows will be thinner and softer, with her right brow raised toward the baby. Grandpa’s brows will be thick and bushy in brass-gray, slightly level.

Grandpa’s eyebrows will be level and slightly raised, suggesting a surprised-proud expression. The teen’s brows will be thin and dark: flat on the left, slightly raised on the right toward the dog, hinting at reluctant amusement. The kid’s brow over the open eye will arch high in mischief; the winked eye will have no brow. The baby and dog will have no eyebrows.

A tiny raised spot above the dog’s eyes will suggest eagerness. Subtle pink blushes will appear on mom, kid, baby and grandpa’s cheeks for warmth, while dad keeps his oil highlight and the teen gets a faint cool blush to show embarrassment. Dad’s wide eyes will show a hint of sclera around his pupils. The script should stay under one thousand lines.

A shadow helper will draw soft floor ellipses at absolute coordinates. The merged family shadow sits at (820, 890) with a wide ellipse. The teen’s shadow is separate at (210, 890). The dog’s shadow at (400, 920) bridges the gap between them.

The teen shadow spans 125–275 and the dog shadow spans 300–500, leaving only a narrow gap between them. The family shadow at x=860 bridges that space slightly. Because the dog sits between the teen and the family, the teen is almost physically connected to the family through the dog. The body separation remains the main narrative clue, so the subtle shadow overlap is acceptable.

A darker contact shadow will sit directly under each pair of feet so the figures look grounded. A radial vignette will fade the edges toward a dark gray, and a soft right-side light source will cast a warm glow across the scene.

A soft white wash at 0.14 opacity will be layered above the vignette to unify the photo, with opacity tuned to avoid color loss. Catchlights will sit on the upper right of each pupil to echo the softbox. A thin rim light is too difficult to draw, so a top-right highlight ellipse on each head will serve that purpose.

A soft double-line seam will run through the gap between the teen and grandpa. A folded paper corner will peek from the top right, and two small clamps will hold the paper at the top left and right. A subtle wrinkle curve will add texture. The SVG is ready to be written.

A wooden stool will sit beside grandpa. Its seat is a foreshortened ellipse with wider hips, and its legs splay downward with a foot ring. One leg will sit slightly off the ground to make the seat tilt, giving the impression of a slightly unstable drawing.

The stool seat will tilt -4 degrees so the crookedness is obvious, with all legs touching the floor. Grandpa’s cane will be drawn in a later layer so it appears in front of both dad and grandpa.

The grandpa hand will be drawn twice: first in the base layer, then again in the later layer so its fingers wrap the cane handle. The cane itself will be drawn after that second hand so it appears to pass in front of the hand.

The cane will be drawn entirely in the grandpa group so it passes behind dad. This avoids the complex hand-overlap trick.

The grandpa group will include the cane, drawn after dad so it passes in front of dad’s legs. The kid will be drawn last to cover any overlap with the cable. A floor cable from the teen’s hip down toward the center and ending in a plug will sit on the ground between the teen and dog.

The cable will be drawn before the dog so the dog sits on it. This makes the cable a trapped headphone or charging cord. The dog is sitting on the teen's equipment.

The cable will be the teen’s unplugged charging cord, dangling from headphones around his neck. The dog sits on it. I am ready to write the SVG and a preview script.

The script will write the SVG to output/awkward-robot-family.svg and build/preview.html, keeping preview.html out of output/. It will add an XML declaration and SVG namespace. A root group will set stroke-linejoin and stroke-linecap to round. A solid background rectangle will be drawn first to prevent transparency.

The baby’s left bootie is steel blue and the right is copper, dangling visibly at the bottom of the dress. The kid’s arms are mismatched: the rabbit-ear arm is dad-blue, while the other arm is copper and akimbo on the hip. This contrast reinforces a showboat personality.

The kid’s overalls will be blue with one shoulder strap undone, letting the copper arm show through. Small scuff marks will sit on his knees. A bandage will rest on his cheek. His propeller hat will sit at an angle. All anchor positions will be gathered into a top constant section for easy editing.

The `bone()` helper will draw each limb segment as a centered rectangle. Joints will be drawn after both bones so their circles cover any gap or overlap at the bend. The arm sequence is upper bone, lower bone, elbow, shoulder, wrist, then hand. The shoulder joint placement relative to the torso is still being decided.

Shoulders will be drawn as part of the arms, sitting on top of the torso. The drawing order is legs first, then torso covering them, then arms, then head and face. Dad’s hanging hand will sit beside his leg in front, drawn after the torso. The embracing arm will be a separate element drawn later.

Mom’s dress will be drawn over her legs so only her feet peek out. Grandpa’s sitting pose is being refined: his thigh angle is too steep for a comfortable seat, so the hip-to-knee distance needs adjustment to read as a relaxed front-view seat.

Grandpa’s sitting pose is being refined for a clear front-view read. The knee will sit at y=-130, just 70 pixels below the hip at y=-200, so the thigh foreshortens naturally toward the camera. Shins will drop straight down to y=-30, and feet will point forward or outward.

Grandpa’s knees will be drawn as 22-pixel circles so the sitting pose is unmistakable. The stool seat ellipse must be wider than the body’s hip width so it peeks out behind and beside the figure, making the seat look too small.

Grandpa’s hips are narrow. The seat ellipse will be drawn with a large vertical radius so its front lip shows between his thighs. His body slightly overhangs the seat on each side, and the legs will sit inside his feet to create the classic too-small-stool effect.

The seat will be a small front arc between the thighs rather than a wide disc. The legs will sit close together and one will peek out between his feet, making the seat look too small.

The stool will be offset 25 pixels left so it peeks out behind grandpa’s hip. He is sliding off-center and hanging off the right side, making the too-small seat read as a slight lean. I am ready to write the SVG.

The light pool will sit at x=720, y=400, centered on the family rather than the canvas. This leaves the right side dimmer and more abandoned, while the softbox glow stays bright. The misplaced lighting reinforces the awkward composition.

The softbox at x=1480 will serve as a rim light rather than a front flash, so the subjects remain evenly lit and the family is not darkened. Six to eight low-opacity, seeded teal ellipses will be added to the backdrop to mimic studio muslin blotches and prevent a flat digital look. The dog’s inside-out ear will reveal its copper-pink interior.

The dog’s head will be rotated -35 degrees to look toward the teen, while its body faces slightly forward at -10 degrees. This creates a 3/4 profile view where both eyes remain visible. The face will be drawn with eyes shifted left and a left-side muzzle ellipse to sell the backward glance.

The dog’s body will be built from local ellipses for the haunch, chest, and back. One hind leg will splay outward to the right, with a visible paw and tail spring on the same side. The head will sit at (-20, -150) and rotate -25 degrees. Paw details will use small ovals with toe lines. A burgundy collar with a blank brass-tag pendant will hang around the neck.

The dog’s right eye will be blown out toward the softbox, rendered as solid white with a faint iris ghost and a small starflare. The left eye stays normal and looks at the teen.

The dog’s eye will stay normal and look at the teen. A subtle catchlight may hit one eye harder, but the love remains clear. The flash-blown-out gag is reserved for grandpa’s cloudy eye and dad’s dead pixel instead.

The teen’s head will turn clockwise toward the dog, while his body leans counterclockwise away. His pupils will be offset down-right so the viewer can trace an eyeline to the dog. I will check that the lines connect in the preview and adjust as needed.

The teen’s head will turn toward the dog and family, while his body leans away from them. Mom’s head will rotate an extra eight degrees clockwise to face the baby, keeping her eyes on the child.

I realized that SVG rotate applies in-plane roll, not yaw. Rotating a head sideways would make it tip rather than turn to look at someone. To show a character looking at another, I should move the pupils instead of rotating the whole head. A slight head tilt can still add emotion without distorting the face.

The teen’s head will tilt slightly away from the dog, and his pupils will aim at the dog. Mom’s head will tilt toward the baby. Dad will stay nearly straight with no roll. Grandpa will sit plumb. The kid will have a playful head roll. The dog’s face will be drawn as a 3/4 profile with asymmetric features rather than relying on a rotation for yaw.

A slight rotation is fine for the dog’s ear flop. All faces will point at the camera, with pupils and head tilts revealing where attention truly lies. Mom’s eyes slide to the baby, the teen’s drop to the dog, the baby’s look upward, and Dad and grandpa lock on.

The teen’s torso will be drawn asymmetrically so one shoulder sits forward and his feet point outward, reinforcing the body’s away-from-the-camera angle. The dog’s body will also be built from local ellipses for its haunch, chest, and back.

The teen’s arms will be crossed and his torso slightly rolled. One foot will point toward the exit as a silhouette tell. Dad and grandpa keep both feet forward. Mom’s feet will lean toward the baby. The kid’s feet will straddle dad’s shoe while one points toward the camera.

The arm-reach math is being recalculated with a smaller mom roll of +3° instead of +6°. The shoulder position now lands near x=968, keeping the pose closer to unrotated while still showing her lean toward the baby.

Dad’s shoulder is at (910, 418). His hand reaches toward the mom’s shoulder at (990, 430), landing just above her neck. The arm angle is nearly horizontal with a slight downward slope.

The dad’s arm will be drawn as a chicken wing. His elbow will sit 48 pixels above his shoulder, with the upper arm rising and the forearm dropping toward her neck. I may raise it further to y=328 for a more dramatic wing pose.

Grandpa’s right shoulder was calculated too close to dad’s left shoulder. I will narrow grandpa’s body width so his shoulder lands around x=640, keeping the two figures separated.

Grandpa’s right shoulder now sits at x=640, only fifty pixels from dad’s left shoulder at x=690. The two figures are close and intimate, slightly cramped. Grandpa’s arm will rest on dad’s shoulder with his hand slightly above it.

The gap between dad and grandpa’s heads is 77 pixels, which feels right for the intended intimacy. The teen will sit at x=230 so his face is not cropped, though his outer elbow will sit close to the edge. I am now calculating his head position with a -6 degree roll, but I need to verify whether the SVG transform applies translation before or after rotation.

I realized the SVG transform applies rotation before translation, so a negative roll tilts the head rightward rather than left. The teen’s head will therefore sit at roughly x=286, not near the left edge.

The teen’s head lands at roughly x=174, fully on the canvas. The outer elbow is now being calculated to sit even farther left.

The teen’s outer elbow still sits inside the canvas at x=75. To create the awkward crop, I will move his position left to x=175. The face will remain visible while the arm is partially cropped.

The teen is now placed at x=190. The dog will sit between the teen and grandpa at x=370, with its floor raised slightly to 935. The baby will stand at x=830, just in front of dad and closer to mom. The adult floor will be set to 900 so their feet have room.

The baby’s floor is now set to 940, leaving a 50-pixel front margin. The canvas top and bottom margins look safe. Rather than locking in every coordinate before previewing, I will use variables and tweak the layout visually after the first screenshot.

I am now writing the SVG code in a single pass. I will skip any README file. The design favors clean, high-quality shapes over excessive rivet detail: grandpa gets eight to ten visible rivets, dad gets two subtle ones under his jaw, and the baby has none. Joint bolts will be rendered as simple circles.

content.text: The family is a studio group that missed its mark: too close in the middle, a gap where the teen stands, and the dog as the only one who bridges it. I'll build that as a single SVG and then check the picture.

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Awkward robot family portrait.

A studio photograph that did not quite work. Gaze, touch, and spacing
carry the relationships; the picture contains no text.

  Grandpa  — proud obsolete unit, enormous earnest eyes, hand heavy on his son
  Dad      — anxious, overdressed, smile one pixel too wide
  Mom      — holding the baby and the shot together; eyes slip at the shutter
  Baby     — new factory model, watching the softbox, fist in mom's cheek
  Kid      — spare parts from both parents, rabbit ears, one foot on dad
  Teen     — body leaving, eyes down on the dog
  Dog      — bought by dad (his tie's color on the collar), devoted to the teen
"""

import math
import os

W, H = 1600, 1000
FLOOR = 900

# Foot / seat anchors
TEEN_X, TEEN_R = 188, -7
DOG_X, DOG_Y = 392, 948
GP_X = 575
DAD_X, DAD_R = 812, 0
MOM_X, MOM_R = 1052, 4
KID_X, KID_Y, KID_R = 868, 952, -3

INK = "#243038"
INK_SOFT = "#243038"

# Metals
DAD = "#4d6b7e"
DAD_D = "#314858"
DAD_L = "#8aa4b4"
DAD_FACE = "#e4ebef"
SHIRT = "#f4f1e8"
SHIRT_S = "#e2ddd0"
TIE = "#8e3b49"
TIE_D = "#6c2c38"
MOM = "#f0b48e"
MOM_D = "#c4815c"
MOM_L = "#f7d4bc"
MOM_FACE = "#f8c9ac"
DRESS = "#c4546c"
DRESS_D = "#993e54"
DRESS_L = "#d9788a"
GP = "#7e8c5a"
GP_D = "#5a663f"
GP_L = "#aeb888"
GP_FACE = "#ead8b6"
BRASS = "#e4c27a"
BRASS_D = "#b58d45"
BRASS_L = "#f3deb0"
KID = "#f0be3a"
KID_D = "#d3981a"
KID_L = "#ffe59a"
KID_FACE = "#ffebc0"
OVR = "#3c7eab"
OVR_D = "#2c6086"
OVR_L = "#6aa4c8"
TEEN = "#2e3138"
TEEN_M = "#3c404a"
TEEN_L = "#555a66"
TEEN_FACE = "#efe8de"
MAG = "#e4548c"
MAG_D = "#b43368"
BABY_C = "#c5ece0"
BABY_D = "#8fcfb8"
BABY_FACE = "#f4fffb"
DOG = "#f6f3ed"
DOG_D = "#d9d2c6"
DOG_SPOT = "#c47b48"
TONGUE = "#ef7d8b"
WOOD = "#a67c52"
WOOD_D = "#7a5436"
SOLE = "#2a2724"


class D:
    def __init__(self):
        self.o = []

    def add(self, t):
        self.o.append(t)

    def g(self, attrs=""):
        self.add(f"<g {attrs}>" if attrs else "<g>")

    def ge(self):
        self.add("</g>")

    def rect(self, x, y, w, h, r, fill, sw=0, stroke=INK, op=1, extra=""):
        so = f' stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{sw}"' if sw else ' stroke="none"'
        oo = f' opacity="{op}"' if op != 1 else ""
        self.add(
            f'<rect x="{x:.1f}" y="{y:.1f}" width="{w:.1f}" height="{h:.1f}" '
            f'rx="{r:.1f}" fill="{fill}"{so}{oo} {extra}/>'
        )

    def ell(self, cx, cy, rx, ry, fill, sw=0, stroke=INK, op=1, extra=""):
        so = f' stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{sw}"' if sw else ' stroke="none"'
        oo = f' opacity="{op}"' if op != 1 else ""
        self.add(
            f'<ellipse cx="{cx:.1f}" cy="{cy:.1f}" rx="{rx:.1f}" ry="{ry:.1f}" '
            f'fill="{fill}"{so}{oo} {extra}/>'
        )

    def circ(self, cx, cy, r, fill, sw=0, stroke=INK, op=1, extra=""):
        self.ell(cx, cy, r, r, fill, sw, stroke, op, extra)

    def line(self, x1, y1, x2, y2, stroke, sw, op=1, cap="round"):
        oo = f' opacity="{op}"' if op != 1 else ""
        self.add(
            f'<line x1="{x1:.1f}" y1="{y1:.1f}" x2="{x2:.1f}" y2="{y2:.1f}" '
            f'stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{sw}" stroke-linecap="{cap}"{oo}/>'
        )

    def path(self, d, fill="none", sw=0, stroke=INK, op=1, extra=""):
        so = f' stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{sw}"' if sw else ' stroke="none"'
        oo = f' opacity="{op}"' if op != 1 else ""
        self.add(f'<path d="{d}" fill="{fill}"{so}{oo} {extra}/>')

    def bone(self, x1, y1, x2, y2, w, fill, sw=3.2):
        ang = math.degrees(math.atan2(y2 - y1, x2 - x1))
        length = math.hypot(x2 - x1, y2 - y1)
        self.add(
            f'<rect x="0" y="{-w / 2:.1f}" width="{length:.1f}" height="{w:.1f}" '
            f'rx="{w / 2:.1f}" fill="{fill}" stroke="{INK}" stroke-width="{sw}" '
            f'transform="translate({x1:.1f},{y1:.1f}) rotate({ang:.2f})"/>'
        )
        # specular streak along the top of the limb
        ox, oy = -math.sin(math.radians(ang)) * (w * 0.22), math.cos(math.radians(ang)) * (w * 0.22)
        # offset toward a consistent "up-left" light by flipping if needed
        self.line(
            x1 + ox * 0.15, y1 + oy * 0.15, x2 + ox * 0.15, y2 + oy * 0.15,
            "#ffffff", max(2.0, w * 0.13), op=0.28,
        )

    def joint(self, x, y, r, fill, bolt=BRASS_D):
        self.circ(x, y, r, fill, sw=3)
        self.circ(x, y, r * 0.38, bolt, sw=1.4)
        self.circ(x - r * 0.12, y - r * 0.14, r * 0.12, "#ffffff", op=0.55)

    def spec(self, cx, cy, rx, ry, op=0.28):
        self.ell(cx, cy, rx, ry, "#ffffff", op=op)

    def shade(self, cx, cy, rx, ry, op=0.13):
        self.ell(cx, cy, rx, ry, "#1a2328", op=op)

    def text_free_badge(self, cx, cy, s=11, fill=BRASS, rot=0, sw=2.2):
        """Family maker's mark: a plain triangle. No lettering."""
        h = s * 1.15
        pts = f"{cx:.1f},{cy - h * 0.62:.1f} {cx - s:.1f},{cy + h * 0.48:.1f} {cx + s:.1f},{cy + h * 0.48:.1f}"
        extra = f'transform="rotate({rot:.1f} {cx:.1f} {cy:.1f})"' if rot else ""
        self.add(
            f'<polygon points="{pts}" fill="{fill}" stroke="{INK}" stroke-width="{sw}" {extra}/>'
        )

    def __str__(self):
        return "\n".join(self.o)


def hand(d, x, y, ang, fill, lengths, spread=9, thick=8, palm=15, thumb=True, thumb_spread=58, sw=2.4):
    """Palm center (x, y). Fingers point along ang (deg, 0=right, -90=up)."""
    a = math.radians(ang)
    n = len(lengths)
    pcx = x
    pcy = y
    # fingers first so the palm caps their bases
    fx = []
    for i, flen in enumerate(lengths):
        off = (i - (n - 1) / 2.0) * (thick + 3.2)
        fa = math.radians(ang + (i - (n - 1) / 2.0) * spread)
        bx = pcx + math.cos(a) * (palm * 0.55) + math.cos(a + math.pi / 2) * off
        by = pcy + math.sin(a) * (palm * 0.55) + math.sin(a + math.pi / 2) * off
        tx = bx + math.cos(fa) * flen
        ty = by + math.sin(fa) * flen
        d.bone(bx, by, tx, ty, thick, fill, sw=sw)
        fx.append((tx, ty))
    d.ell(pcx, pcy, palm, palm * 0.86, fill, sw=sw + 0.4)
    d.spec(pcx - palm * 0.25, pcy - palm * 0.28, palm * 0.28, palm * 0.18, 0.35)
    if thumb:
        ta = math.radians(ang + thumb_spread)
        bx = pcx + math.cos(ta) * palm * 0.2 + math.cos(a + math.pi / 2) * palm * 0.15
        by = pcy + math.sin(ta) * palm * 0.2 + math.sin(a + math.pi / 2) * palm * 0.15
        # place thumb on the side opposite the finger fan's "inner"
        side = thumb_spread / abs(thumb_spread) if thumb_spread else 1
        bx = pcx + math.cos(a + side * math.pi / 2) * palm * 0.72
        by = pcy + math.sin(a + side * math.pi / 2) * palm * 0.72
        tx = bx + math.cos(ta) * palm * 0.95
        ty = by + math.sin(ta) * palm * 0.95
        d.bone(bx, by, tx, ty, thick * 1.05, fill, sw=sw)
    return fx


def eye(d, cx, cy, rx, ry, dx, dy, iris, skin, lid=0.0, cloudy=False, ring="#c5d0d6"):
    """Lid is 0..1 coverage from the top, painted in the face color."""
    d.ell(cx, cy, rx + 6.5, ry + 6.5, INK)
    d.ell(cx, cy, rx + 3.2, ry + 3.2, ring)
    d.ell(cx, cy, rx, ry, "#f5f8f8")
    d.ell(cx + dx, cy + dy, rx * 0.62, ry * 0.66, iris)
    d.ell(cx + dx, cy + dy, rx * 0.30, ry * 0.34, "#16191c")
    # catchlight, upper right — the in-frame softbox
    d.ell(cx + dx + rx * 0.26, cy + dy - ry * 0.30, max(2.2, rx * 0.16), max(1.8, ry * 0.14), "#ffffff")
    d.ell(cx + dx - rx * 0.18, cy + dy + ry * 0.22, max(1.2, rx * 0.07), max(1.0, ry * 0.06), "#ffffff", op=0.7)
    if cloudy:
        d.ell(cx, cy, rx * 0.92, ry * 0.92, "#d5ddd8", op=0.55)
        d.ell(cx + 4, cy + 3, rx * 0.35, ry * 0.22, "#ffffff", op=0.25)
    if lid > 0:
        cover = ry * (0.15 + 1.15 * lid)
        # skin-colored lid cap
        d.path(
            f"M {cx - rx - 7:.1f} {cy + ry * 0.15:.1f} "
            f"Q {cx:.1f} {cy - ry - 8 + cover * 0.15:.1f} {cx + rx + 7:.1f} {cy + ry * 0.15:.1f} "
            f"L {cx + rx + 8:.1f} {cy - ry - 14:.1f} L {cx - rx - 8:.1f} {cy - ry - 14:.1f} Z",
            fill=skin,
        )
        # lash line
        d.path(
            f"M {cx - rx + 1:.1f} {cy - ry * (0.15 + lid * 0.7):.1f} "
            f"Q {cx:.1f} {cy - ry * (0.55 + lid * 0.5):.1f} {cx + rx - 1:.1f} {cy - ry * (0.15 + lid * 0.7):.1f}",
            sw=3.2, stroke=INK,
        )


def brow(d, cx, cy, w, rot, color, thick=7):
    d.add(
        f'<rect x="{cx - w / 2:.1f}" y="{cy - thick / 2:.1f}" width="{w:.1f}" height="{thick:.1f}" '
        f'rx="{thick / 2:.1f}" fill="{color}" stroke="{INK}" stroke-width="1.6" '
        f'transform="rotate({rot:.1f} {cx:.1f} {cy:.1f})"/>'
    )


def vent_nose(d, cx, cy, s=1.0, color=None):
    color = color or INK
    for i, w in enumerate((16, 12, 8)):
        ww = w * s
        d.rect(cx - ww / 2, cy + i * 6.2 * s, ww, 3.1 * s, 1.4 * s, color, sw=1.2)


def button_nose(d, cx, cy, r=7, fill=None):
    fill = fill or "#e09878"
    d.circ(cx, cy, r, fill, sw=2.2)
    d.circ(cx - r * 0.28, cy - r * 0.32, r * 0.28, "#ffffff", op=0.65)


def rivet(d, x, y, r=4.2, fill=BRASS):
    d.circ(x, y, r, fill, sw=1.6)
    d.line(x - r * 0.5, y, x + r * 0.5, y, BRASS_D, 1.2)


def studio(d):
    # Muslin sweep. Cool, a little tired, lighter behind the cluster
    # (they missed the mark, which sits further right).
    d.rect(0, 0, W, H, "#5e7c86")
    d.ell(760, 380, 620, 460, "#86a4ac", op=0.55)
    d.ell(700, 340, 340, 280, "#c3d4d4", op=0.22)
    d.ell(-40, 80, 380, 320, "#3e5962", op=0.28)
    d.ell(1680, 60, 420, 300, "#3a5360", op=0.25)
    d.ell(200, 520, 260, 180, "#6d8e96", op=0.18)
    d.ell(1100, 180, 220, 160, "#78969e", op=0.16)
    d.ell(1420, 460, 280, 220, "#4c6872", op=0.20)
    # blotches — painted muslin, not a flat ramp
    blot = [
        (280, 160, 90, 50, 0.07),
        (520, 90, 120, 40, 0.06),
        (900, 140, 80, 36, 0.05),
        (1240, 220, 100, 46, 0.07),
        (640, 260, 70, 30, 0.05),
        (1040, 80, 90, 34, 0.06),
    ]
    for x, y, rx, ry, op in blot:
        d.ell(x, y, rx, ry, "#d5e4e4", op=op)
        d.ell(x + 30, y + 18, rx * 0.6, ry * 0.5, "#3e5962", op=op)

    # Unfortunate seam in the gap between the teen and grandpa.
    d.path(
        "M392 0 C 404 80, 378 160, 396 260 C 414 360, 372 460, 390 560 C 400 620, 384 660, 392 720",
        sw=14, stroke="#6e9096", op=0.35,
    )
    d.path(
        "M402 0 C 414 80, 388 160, 406 260 C 424 360, 382 460, 400 560 C 410 620, 394 660, 402 720",
        sw=3, stroke="#e4f0f0", op=0.35,
    )

    # Floor of the sweep, warmer where the strobe hits.

            f'<rect x="{x:.1f}" y="{y:.1f}" width="{w:.1f}" height="{h:.1f}" '

    def ell(self, cx, cy, rx, ry, fill, sw=0, stroke=INK, op=1, extra=""):

        oo = f' opacity="{op}"' if op != 1 else ""
        self.add(
            f'<ellipse cx="{cx:.1f}" cy="{cy:.1f}" rx="{rx:.1f}" ry="{ry:.1f}" '

def build():
    d = D()
    d.add(
        f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{W}" height="{H}" '
        f'viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round">'
    )
    d.add(defs())
    studio(d)
    shadows(d)
    dad_body(d)
    grandpa(d)
    mom_and_baby(d)
    dad_arm(d)
    teen(d)
    kid(d)
    dog(d)
    grade(d)
    d.add("</svg>")
    return "\n".join(d.o) + "\n"


def main():
    root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    out = os.path.join(root, "output", "awkward-robot-family.svg")
    svg = build()
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out), exist_ok=True)
    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(svg)
    preview = os.path.join(root, "build", "preview.html")
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(preview), exist_ok=True)
    with open(preview, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(
            "<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset='utf-8'><style>"
            "html,body{margin:0;padding:0;background:#222;}svg{display:block;}"
            "</style></head><body>\n"

        by = pcy + math.sin(ta) * palm * 0.2 + math.sin(a + math.pi / 2) * palm * 0.15

        tx = bx + math.cos(ta) * palm * 0.95
        ty = by + math.sin(ta) * palm * 0.95
        d.bone(bx, by, tx, ty, thick * 1.05, fill, sw=sw)

content.thinking:
The image rendered, but the composition and anatomy need fixing.

Grandpa is standing with a raised arm and a long cane line across the floor. The kid's arm extends downward through the frame instead of upward to dad's head.

The kid's local Y axis points upward, so positive values extend downward through the floor. Dad's head sits at y=-778 in his local space, which is above the kid's translated position at y=952.

The kid's arm must rise to roughly local y=-780 to reach dad's head. Dad's head center sits at local x=-56 relative to the kid, and the kid's slight rotation must be factored into the alignment.

The rabbit ears should sit near local (-20, -800), just above and slightly right of dad's head. Dad's arm resting on mom's shoulder looks like a claw, which is the intended pose. Mom's reaching hand may accidentally rest on the kid's shoulder.

Mom's reaching hand resting on the kid's shoulder reads as a gentle touch, so that pose will be kept and refined. Baby's wide eyes need a stronger upward gaze to look directly at the viewer. Teen's pose is solid with crossed arms and headphones, though his eyes may not clearly focus on the dog.

The dog is too small and lost among the family. It should be slightly larger to read as an attentive pet.
